title: Attention Is All You Need
note: Self-attention lets every token combine information from other tokens. Multi-head attention learns different relationships; positional encodings supply order. Compare attention cost with recurrent models.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
note: Masked language modelling learns bidirectional representations. Fine-tuning adapts the encoder to downstream tasks. Contrast masked-token training with autoregressive next-token prediction.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
note: Scaling autoregressive language models enables in-context task demonstrations. Few-shot prompting changes the context without updating weights. Distinguish in-context learning from fine-tuning.

title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
short: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning (T5)
note: A unified text-to-text format expresses many NLP tasks with one interface. The paper compares pretraining choices and transfer settings. Study span corruption and encoder-decoder generation.

title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
note: Training choices substantially affect BERT performance. More data, longer training and dynamic masking improve the recipe. An architectural change is not always needed for a stronger baseline.

title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding
note: Permutation language modelling combines autoregressive objectives with access to varied context orders. Two-stream attention avoids leaking the prediction target. Compare its objective with BERT masking.

title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
note: Factorised embeddings and cross-layer parameter sharing reduce parameter count. Sentence-order prediction supplies a pretraining signal. Parameter savings do not automatically imply proportional compute savings.

title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
note: A bidirectional encoder and autoregressive decoder reconstruct corrupted text. Denoising pretraining supports generation tasks. Compare reconstruction with T5 span corruption.

title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer
note: Locality-sensitive hashing approximates attention and reversible layers reduce activation memory. Efficiency comes with approximation and implementation trade-offs. Separate memory complexity from wall-clock speed.

title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
note: Local sliding-window attention combines with selected global attention positions. This enables longer documents without full quadratic attention. Global-token choice matters for the task.

title: Rethinking Attention with Performers
note: Random-feature approximations estimate softmax attention with linear scaling. Approximation quality depends on feature construction and count. Compare approximate attention with exact kernel optimisations.

title: Linformer: Self-Attention with Linear Complexity
note: Low-rank projections compress the sequence dimension of keys and values. The method reduces attention complexity under a low-rank hypothesis. Ask how sequence length and projection rank affect fidelity.

title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
note: Tiling and online softmax reduce memory traffic for exact attention. The central insight is hardware-aware IO efficiency. It does not replace exact attention with a sparse approximation.

title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
note: Improved work partitioning and parallelism increase attention throughput. The method retains exact attention while changing GPU execution. Hardware utilisation matters alongside asymptotic complexity.

title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
note: Rotary position embeddings rotate query and key vectors to encode positions. Their dot products incorporate relative positional structure. Separate position representation from attention sparsity.

title: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation
note: Attention logits receive head-specific linear distance biases. This avoids learned positional embeddings and studies length extrapolation. Extrapolation performance is an empirical question.

title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
note: Segment-level recurrence reuses previous hidden states. Relative positional encodings help maintain temporal consistency across segments. Reused states extend context without backpropagating through all history.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
short: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
note: Model size, data and compute exhibit empirical power-law relationships with loss. Compute allocation becomes a design problem. These fitted laws describe specific training regimes rather than universal guarantees.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
note: Jointly scaling training data and parameters changes compute-optimal model design. The work challenges recipes with large models trained on too few tokens. Compare a fixed compute budget across configurations.

title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
note: Large-scale dense language modelling studies scaling across many tasks. Architecture and distributed training choices support the model. Examine multilingual performance and evaluation limitations separately.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
note: Training open foundation models on public data emphasises inference-efficient model sizes. More training tokens can improve smaller models. Compare training cost with deployment cost.

title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
note: Pretraining and dialogue alignment produce a family of language models. Supervised tuning and preference optimisation shape chat behaviour. Separate base-model capability from alignment effects.

title: Mistral 7B
note: Grouped-query and sliding-window attention support efficient inference. Model quality depends on both training and architecture. Inspect which attention mechanisms are actually used in a checkpoint.

title: Mixtral of Experts
note: Sparse expert routing activates only a subset of feed-forward networks per token. Total parameters differ from active parameters. Routing, memory and communication affect practical efficiency.

title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
note: Simplified sparse routing scales model capacity while limiting per-token computation. Load balancing and training stability are central challenges. Compare dense compute with expert capacity.

title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
note: A sparsely gated mixture-of-experts layer routes examples to selected experts. Conditional computation increases capacity without activating all weights. Load imbalance can erase theoretical efficiency gains.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
note: Low-rank matrices represent weight updates while pretrained weights remain frozen. Training fewer parameters reduces optimiser memory. Distinguish low-rank adaptation from low-rank compression of the base model.

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
note: Quantisation of frozen base weights combines with low-rank adapters. Quantisation-aware storage and paged optimisers reduce fine-tuning memory. Check training memory separately from inference performance.

title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
note: Small trainable modules adapt a frozen pretrained model. Task-specific parameters are stored separately. Compare adapter placement with LoRA weight updates.

title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
note: Trainable continuous prefixes steer a frozen model. The learned prefix differs from a human-written text prompt. Compare prefix length, task performance and trainable parameter count.

title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
short: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
note: Soft prompt embeddings adapt frozen language models. Their effectiveness changes with model scale. Prompt tuning and full fine-tuning have different storage and training costs.

title: BitFit: Simple Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning for Transformer-based Masked Language-models
note: Updating only bias terms can provide a parameter-efficient adaptation baseline. Its strength varies by task and data regime. Simple baselines help test whether a more complex method is needed.

title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
note: Weight decomposition separates magnitude from direction during adaptation. Low-rank updates operate on direction with additional magnitude learning. Compare gains against LoRA under matched budgets.

title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
note: A clipped surrogate objective discourages excessively large policy updates. On-policy samples estimate policy gradients and advantages. Clipping is a practical stabiliser, not a strict trust-region guarantee.

title: Trust Region Policy Optimization
note: Policy improvement is constrained using a KL-divergence trust region. Approximate optimisation makes the update tractable. Compare the explicit constraint with PPO clipping.

title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning
short: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DQN)
note: A neural network estimates action values from pixels. Experience replay reduces correlations in training samples. Distinguish value-based control from direct policy optimisation.

title: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning
short: Continuous Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DDPG)
note: An actor-critic method combines deterministic policy gradients and replay. Target networks support more stable learning. Continuous actions require a different maximisation strategy from discrete DQN.

title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor
note: Maximum-entropy reinforcement learning rewards both return and policy entropy. Off-policy training reuses experience. The entropy coefficient controls an exploration-performance trade-off.

title: Addressing Function Approximation Error in Actor-Critic Methods
short: Addressing Function Approximation Error in Actor-Critic Methods (TD3)
note: Twin critics, delayed policy updates and target smoothing reduce overestimation problems. Critic error can propagate into poor policies. Compare these mechanisms individually through ablations.

title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
note: Exponentially weighted temporal-difference residuals estimate advantages. A lambda parameter trades bias against variance. Advantage estimation is distinct from the policy-update objective.

title: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning
short: Asynchronous Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning (A3C)
note: Parallel actor-learners decorrelate experience and update a shared model. Actor-critic training combines policy and value learning. Compare asynchronous sampling with replay-based approaches.

title: Rainbow: Combining Improvements in Deep Reinforcement Learning
note: Several DQN improvements are combined and studied through ablations. Distributional learning, prioritisation and multi-step returns address different issues. Combined performance does not identify each component's contribution.

title: Hindsight Experience Replay
note: Failed goal-conditioned trajectories can be relabelled with achieved goals. Sparse rewards become more informative. Relabelling depends on a compatible goal and reward formulation.

title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling
note: Offline reinforcement learning is formulated as sequence modelling conditioned on desired return. A causal transformer predicts actions from trajectories. Dataset coverage constrains what the learned policy can do.

title: Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences
short: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
note: Pairwise human comparisons train a reward model for policy learning. Preference labels replace direct reward engineering. Reward-model errors can be amplified by optimisation.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
short: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions (InstructGPT)
note: Supervised demonstrations and human preferences align language-model outputs. A learned reward model guides policy optimisation. Helpfulness and truthfulness require separate evaluation.

title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
note: A preference objective directly updates a language model relative to a reference policy. The formulation avoids an explicit online RL loop. Preference data quality and reference choice still matter.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
note: Written principles guide critique, revision and preference-based alignment. AI feedback can reduce some human labelling needs. The chosen principles encode normative assumptions.

title: Learning to summarize from human feedback
short: Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback
note: Human comparisons train reward models for summarisation. Optimising preference reward can improve judged quality. Evaluate factuality separately from preference scores.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
note: Worked intermediate reasoning examples can improve performance on multi-step tasks. The method changes the prompt without updating model weights. A plausible explanation is not proof of correct reasoning.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
short: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning
note: Multiple sampled reasoning paths vote on a final answer. Diversity can improve reliability at additional inference cost. Agreement can still preserve shared mistakes.

title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
short: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
note: A simple reasoning cue can elicit intermediate steps without worked demonstrations. Performance depends on model and task. Check answers rather than trusting fluent steps.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
note: Language-model reasoning interleaves with actions and observations. External tools supply evidence and state changes. Tool outputs must be validated and treated as data.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
note: Search explores and evaluates multiple intermediate reasoning states. Branching and backtracking extend linear chain-of-thought prompting. Better results can require substantially more inference.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
note: A language model learns when and how to call tools from generated examples. Tool use is incorporated into language-model training. Separate tool-call correctness from final-answer quality.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
note: Verbal feedback is stored to improve later attempts. This resembles an external memory loop rather than gradient-based learning. Feedback quality limits iterative improvement.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
short: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
note: A retriever supplies passages to a generator. Retrieval allows external knowledge to support answers without storing everything in parameters. Evaluate retrieval recall and grounded generation separately.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
note: Dual encoders map questions and passages into a shared vector space. Inner-product search retrieves relevant passages. Negative-sampling choices influence retrieval quality.

title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
note: Token-level embeddings support late interaction between queries and documents. This retains finer matching than a single vector per document. Index size and query latency are key trade-offs.

title: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens
short: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens (RETRO)
note: Retrieved text chunks condition language modelling during training and inference. External memory changes the relationship between parameters and knowledge. Consider corpus contamination and retrieval cost.

title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
short: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE)
note: A generated hypothetical document becomes the query representation for dense retrieval. The generated text is a search aid, not verified evidence. Retrieved sources must still support the answer.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
note: Reflection tokens help a model decide when to retrieve and assess support. Retrieval and generation are coordinated through training. Citation presence alone does not establish citation correctness.

title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
short: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach
note: Entity relationships and hierarchical community summaries support global corpus questions. Graph construction adds a preprocessing stage. Compare local fact lookup with corpus-wide thematic synthesis.

title: Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models
short: Generalization through Memorization: Nearest Neighbor Language Models
note: Nearest-neighbour retrieval over a datastore augments language-model predictions. Nonparametric memory can adapt knowledge without retraining all weights. Datastore construction influences cost and relevance.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks
note: A generator and discriminator learn through an adversarial objective. The generator tries to match the data distribution. Training instability and mode collapse motivate later variants.

title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
note: A variational bound trains a probabilistic latent-variable model. The reparameterisation trick enables gradient estimates. Reconstruction and latent regularisation pull in different directions.

title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks
note: Convolutional architectural choices improve adversarial image modelling. Learned features can transfer to other tasks. Architecture and optimisation choices influence GAN stability.

title: Wasserstein GAN
note: An alternative distribution distance supplies a critic-based training objective. A Lipschitz constraint is central to the formulation. The original weight-clipping implementation has limitations.

title: Improved Training of Wasserstein GANs
note: A gradient penalty replaces weight clipping to constrain the critic. This can improve training behaviour. The penalty is applied on sampled interpolations rather than everywhere.

title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
short: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for GANs (StyleGAN)
note: A mapping network and layer-wise style controls separate aspects of image generation. Noise models stochastic details. Latent controls are not guaranteed to be perfectly disentangled.

title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
note: A forward noise process is reversed by learned denoising steps. The training objective connects to denoising score matching. Sampling quality and sampling cost must be considered together.

title: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
note: Alternative reverse processes reuse a diffusion training objective. Deterministic sampling paths can reduce the number of generation steps. Fewer steps can change quality.

title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
short: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
note: Stochastic differential equations unify continuous-time diffusion and score models. Reverse dynamics use learned scores. Numerical solvers affect generation speed and quality.

title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
short: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
note: Diffusion operates in a learned latent space instead of raw pixels. Cross-attention supports conditioning. Autoencoder reconstruction sets a practical limit on preserved detail.

title: Classifier-Free Diffusion Guidance
note: Conditional and unconditional predictions are combined during sampling. Guidance strength trades diversity against prompt adherence. Larger guidance is not uniformly better.

title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
note: Transformer backbones replace common convolutional diffusion architectures. Patchified latent inputs enable scaling experiments. Compare compute budgets as well as parameter counts.

title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
short: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
note: A gradual noising process is paired with a learned reverse process. This early diffusion formulation motivates later denoising models. Study the connection between transitions and likelihood bounds.

title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
short: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (ResNet)
note: Skip connections let layers learn residual functions. They ease optimisation of very deep networks. Residual connections differ from simply adding more layers.

title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
note: Stacks of small convolutions build deep image representations. Depth and regular architecture are the central ideas. High parameter and compute costs matter in deployment.

title: Going Deeper with Convolutions
note: Parallel convolutional branches capture multiple receptive-field scales. Bottleneck projections control computation. Compare branch design with a uniform sequential stack.

title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
note: Each layer receives features from preceding layers through concatenation. Feature reuse changes gradient flow and memory requirements. Concatenation is different from residual addition.

title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
note: An encoder-decoder network uses skip connections for precise localisation. It was developed for biomedical segmentation. Pixel-level predictions require different evaluation from image classification.

title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
note: Object detection is framed as a single regression problem. Joint prediction supports fast inference. Compare localisation errors, small-object performance and throughput.

title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
note: A region-proposal network shares convolutional features with detection. Learned proposals replace an external proposal stage. Two-stage and one-stage detectors have different speed-quality trade-offs.

title: Mask R-CNN
note: An instance-mask branch extends region-based object detection. RoIAlign reduces misalignment from feature quantisation. Instance segmentation separates individual objects, not just semantic classes.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
note: Image patches become tokens for a transformer encoder. Pretraining scale strongly influences performance. Compare inductive biases with convolutional networks.

title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
note: Shifted local windows build hierarchical visual representations efficiently. Window shifts enable cross-window communication. Hierarchy supports dense prediction as well as classification.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
short: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (CLIP)
note: Contrastive learning aligns image and text representations. Text descriptions support zero-shot classification. Performance depends on prompts, data and distribution shift.

title: Segment Anything
note: Promptable segmentation supports different user inputs through a shared model. A large data-collection process is central to the approach. Segmentation masks do not by themselves provide semantic understanding.

title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
note: A lightweight querying transformer bridges frozen vision and language models. Staged training aligns representations for generation. Frozen backbones reduce trainable parameters but retain inference cost.

title: Visual Instruction Tuning
note: Visual features are connected to a language model and tuned with multimodal instructions. Instruction data shapes interaction behaviour. Evaluate visual grounding rather than fluency alone.

title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
note: Gated cross-attention conditions language generation on visual inputs. Interleaved image-text examples support few-shot tasks. Visual encoding and language generation remain distinct components.

title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
short: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning (SimCLR)
note: Augmented views of the same image form positive pairs. Contrastive training depends heavily on augmentation and batch design. Representation quality is measured through downstream evaluation.

title: Bootstrap your own latent: A new approach to self-supervised Learning
note: An online network predicts a slowly updated target network's representations. Explicit negative pairs are not required. Architectural asymmetry and training dynamics matter for avoiding collapse.

title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
note: A queue and momentum encoder maintain a consistent dictionary for contrastive learning. This decouples dictionary size from batch size. Stale representations are an important design consideration.

title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
short: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers (DINO)
note: Self-distillation learns visual features without manual labels. Teacher updates and multi-crop views guide training. Emergent attention patterns are qualitative observations, not segmentation guarantees.

title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
short: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
note: A high fraction of image patches is masked and reconstructed. An asymmetric encoder-decoder reduces pretraining cost. Reconstruction targets influence learned representations.

title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
short: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
note: Neighbourhood aggregation combines graph structure with node features. Layer stacking propagates information over multiple hops. Oversmoothing and transductive assumptions deserve attention.

title: Graph Attention Networks
note: Learned attention weights aggregate neighbouring node features. Attention is computed within graph neighbourhoods. Weights are not automatically causal explanations.

title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
short: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs (GraphSAGE)
note: Neighbour sampling and aggregation learn embeddings for unseen nodes. The method supports inductive use beyond a fixed training graph. Sampling introduces a computation-variance trade-off.
